projects.name: Scalable, interpretable, and privacy-preserving feature engineering for federated learning: a systematic literature review
projects.description: This systematic review synthesizes 74 studies from 2020–2025 on feature engineering and feature selection across centralized, horizontal federated, vertical federated, and hybrid learning. It examines interpretability, privacy, fairness, compute and communication costs, and reproducibility, and identifies gaps in pipeline-level privacy accounting, end-to-end evaluation, and standardized benchmarks. The GUI provides a reproducible horizontal-federated synthetic experiment, labeled CSV processing, and single-record prediction from a synthetic-trained model using a named feature library, private feature ranking, model metrics, and a group-recall diagnostic. It is an educational simulation, not secure distributed training; only the feature-ranking query has a differential-privacy guarantee.
projects.publication_citation: Vijay Kumar Kambhampati and K. B. V. Brahma Rao. Scalable, interpretable, and privacy-preserving feature engineering for federated learning: a systematic literature review. Evolving Systems 17, 92 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1007/s12530-026-09852-8
